Article 14

Article 13
In implementing the obligation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children, the Regional Government shall establish an Integrated Service Center (PPT) institution

CHAPTER VII
EMPOWERMENT OF VICTIMS
Article 22
Empowerment of Gender and Child Victims of Violence is implemented in the form of:
a. Empowerment of gender-based violence victims includes job training, productive economic enterprises and joint business groups with capital assistance.
b. Empowerment of child victims of violence who are not in school is to ensure child victims of violence receive the right to continue their education, and/or receive job training with capital assistance.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Pekalongan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the Regent and Regional Apparatus as elements of regional government administration.
3. Agency for Community Empowerment, Women and Family Planning hereinafter referred to as BPMPKB is the Agency for Community Empowerment, Women and Family Planning of Pekalongan Regency as the institution for formulating and implementing regional policies that are specific in the field of community empowerment, women and family planning.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
5. Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
6. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
7. Gender Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, regional government, or other parties who know or hear that violence against men or women will or has occurred either temporarily or based on court determination.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
10. Violence against children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which include but are not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
11. Victims of gender-based violence are people who because of their gender experience physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from State policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
12. Integrated Services are a series of activities to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out jointly by relevant agencies or institutions as one unified implementation, prevention efforts, health services, psychosocial rehabilitation, repatriation, social reintegration, and legal assistance for victims of gender-based violence and children.
13. Companion is a person or institution and/or body that has the expertise to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Integrated Service Center hereinafter abbreviated as PPT is a unified unit that organizes integrated services for women and children victims of violence.
15. Medical Services are facilities that provide services that are clinical in nature in the field of diagnostics, and/or inpatient care for victims.
16. Social rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial condition disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning both in the family and in society.
17. Legal Aid is the provision of legal assistance to victims seeking justice who are unable and face difficulties in the legal field outside or before the court without compensation.
18. Repatriation is the act of returning victims to their region of origin or country of origin while prioritizing protection services and fulfillment of their needs.
19. Social Reintegration is the reunification of victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
20. Safe House is a shelter for victims, during the assistance process, for the safety and comfort of victims from threats and dangers of perpetrators.
21. Service Standards are benchmarks used as guidelines for service delivery and reference for assessing service quality as obligations and promises of organizers to the community in the context of quality, appropriate, easy, affordable and measurable services.
22. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in direct lineage upward or downward up to the third degree.
23. Household is husband, wife, and children, people who have family relationships due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and representation, and/or domestic workers and reside in that household.
24. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget hereinafter abbreviated as APBD is the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of Pekalongan Regency.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing tribe, religion, race, class, gender, ethnicity, culture and language, legal status and physical or mental condition.
Letter b What is meant by "best interests of the victim" is that all actions concerning victims carried out by the government, community, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, the best interests of the victim must be the primary consideration.
Letter c What is meant by "gender justice" is fair treatment given to both women and men.
What is meant by "gender equality" is a condition and position that describes a harmonious, aligned and balanced relationship between men and women in obtaining opportunities/chances in access, participation, control and benefits in the implementation of development as well as enjoying the results of development in family life, as well as in community, national and state life.
Letter d What is meant by "victim protection" is providing a sense of security to victims carried out by family members, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
Letter e What is meant by "maternal survival" is ensuring that a mother does not experience death that occurs during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum, whether caused by physical or non-physical conditions.
Letter f What is meant by "growth and development" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to education, the right to play, the right to create and recreate.
What is meant by "survival" of children is as stated in the principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including the right to identity and the right to enjoy the highest attainable health status.
Letter g. What is meant by "respect for the views of the child" is respect for children's rights to participate and express their opinions in decision-making, especially if it concerns matters that affect their lives.
Letter h What is meant by "openness" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is transparent among the integrated service providers.
Letter i What is meant by "integration" is that in the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children it is carried out by building coordination among service providers, including medical services, legal advocates, psychologists, religious counselors, social workers, police.
Letter j What is meant by "not blaming the victim" is an attitude and treatment of not blaming the victim for the occurrence of violence experienced by them.
Letter k What is meant by "empowering" is that every effort provided must be able to strengthen the victim, whether physically, psychologically, socially or economically.
Letter l What is meant by "victim confidentiality" is every action taken to ensure the victim is in a safe condition from threats or other actions that threaten the life and psychological state of the victim.
Letter m What is meant by "decision-making in the hands of the victim" is the victim's right to determine the best choice in resolving their problem.

I. GENERAL
Acts of violence against women and children constitute violations of human rights; therefore their dignity and honor need to be protected and their right to life guaranteed in accordance with their nature and natural condition, without discrimination.
In order to prevent and address gender-based violence and violence against children in Pekalongan Regency so as to avoid violence, threats of violence, torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and honor, it is necessary to provide protection for women and children who are victims of violence in the form of a Regional Regulation. Thus far, laws and regulations governing the protection of women and children who are victims of violence have not yet regulated protection efforts at the regional level; therefore, institutional support and regulations are needed that can guarantee its implementation.
This Regional Regulation regulates protection efforts for victims, particularly in terms of prevention, services, and empowerment for women and children who are victims of violence in Pekalongan Regency.

Article 21
(1) The procedures and mechanisms for the establishment of PPT shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.
(2) The Service Standards of PPT shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER XI
TRANSITIONAL PROVISIONS
Article 26
In the event of a change in the structure of Regional Apparatus Organizations, the task of coordinating guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children as referred to in Article 23 paragraph (2) shall be carried out by the Regional Apparatus that oversees Women's Empowerment and Children.

Article 3
The purpose of providing protection to victims of gender-based violence is to provide services and protection to male and female victims of gender-based violence and child victims of violence that occurs within the household and/or outside the household.

Article 11
Maltreatment as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter f is caused by:
a. any act or action, whether intentional or unintentional, committed by another person that makes an individual sick or disturbed in their feelings, or causes them to experience unpleasant feelings that make someone sad, disappointed, annoyed, angry and afraid.
b. any sexual violation committed or permitted to be committed against a young person by an adult or another person legally responsible for them, including touching a child with the intention of sexual gratification or forcing a child to touch an adult, sexual intercourse, showing sexual activities to a child, pornography or allowing a child to engage in sexual intercourse that is not appropriate to their development.

CHAPTER VIII
GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION
Article 23
(1) The Regional Government conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and child victims.
(2) The implementation of guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out on a daily basis by BPMPKB.

CHAPTER IX
FUNDING
Article 24
Funding for the implementation of protection activities for victims of gender-based violence and child victims carried out by the Regional Government is sourced from the APBD, Provincial APBD and/or APBN as well as other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

6.5.rationale: Reviewing the Indonesian text, there is no explicit mention of persons with disabilities (penyandang disabilitas/difabel) as a target group, nor any disability-specific measures. The only relevant language is in the elucidation of Pasal 2 huruf a (non-discrimination): protection is provided "tanpa membedakan ... kondisi fisik maupun mental." That is a general non-discrimination statement, not a specific intersectional provision for people with disabilities. The retrieved English candidates include this exact point, and the judge’s rationale (that there are no special disability-targeted measures) matches the Indonesian. Therefore the golden label 'Yes' appears incorrect for this document.

6.7.evaluator_rationale: The non-discrimination principle references tribe, religion, race, ethnicity, culture, and language, but the excerpts do not provide special protection measures specifically targeted at women from minority or isolated groups.

Empowerment of Gender and Child Victims of Violence is implemented in the form of:

Article 24
Funding for the implementation of protection activities for victims of gender-based violence and child victims carried out by the Regional Government is sourced from the APBD, Provincial APBD and/or APBN as well as other lawful sources in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 11
Maltreatment as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter f is caused by:
a. any act or action, whether intentional or unintentional, committed by another person that makes an individual sick or disturbed in their feelings, or causes them to experience unpleasant feelings that make someone sad, disappointed, annoyed, angry and afraid.
b. any sexual violation committed or permitted to be committed against a young person by an adult or another person legally responsible for them, including touching a child with the intention of sexual gratification or forcing a child to touch an adult, sexual intercourse, showing sexual activities to a child, pornography or allowing a child to engage in sexual intercourse that is not appropriate to their development.

Article 10
Exploitation as referred to in Article 5 paragraph (2) letter e occurs due to:
a. acts that exploit economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or another person;
b. acts, with or without the victim’s consent, which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, subjugation, extortion, exploitation of physical, sexual, or reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues, or the use of a person’s labor or abilities by other parties to obtain benefits, whether material or immaterial; and/or
c. all forms of use of the victim’s sexual organs or other body organs to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities or indecent acts.

6.7.rationale: In the Indonesian text, the elucidation of Pasal 2 huruf a defines non-discrimination as protection without distinguishing "suku, agama, ras, golongan, jenis kelamin, etnis, budaya dan bahasa, status hukum dan kondisi fisik maupun mental." This is a general equality/non-discrimination principle; the regulation does not provide specific measures targeted at women from minority/isolated groups (e.g., adat terpencil, minoritas agama/etnis) beyond that general clause. The retrieved English passages contain this non-discrimination language, and the judge correctly concluded there are no special targeted protections. Thus the golden label 'Yes' likely over-codes general non-discrimination as minority-group targeting and appears wrong.
